To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
time scale separation is important for the management of renewable resources and ignoring it may result in inefficiencies and suboptimal management.

1) the time scale separation is a key factor in the evolution of renewable resources; 2) the management rules designed without accounting of time scale separation are inefficient; 3) the management rules that account for time scale separation are efficient.

(a) ignoring time-scale separation can lead to large errors in the optimal regulation of renewable resources; (b) the magnitude of the time-scale separation error depends on the ratio of the two time scales, and (c) the error can be large even when the time scale separation ratio is not large, i.e., even when the two time scales are not widely different.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of renewable resource harvesting in the presence of time scale separation and the implications of time scale externalities in environmental management.
the role of time scales in environmental and economic modeling.
the analysis of time scale separation in renewable resource harvesting and the implications of this separation in optimal management of these resources.
